transcript: An AI model just rediscovered Newton's laws in less than 48 hours, and it wasn't even trained on any existing laws of physics. It's called AI Newton, and it's built by Peking University in China. And they intentionally avoided using ChatGPT or Claude because they already know physics. They give this AI model data from 46 simulated experiments. Think of balls colliding, spring stretching, and objects falling. And no definitions of mass, force, or energy was given. It had to figure them out by studying how things moved. First, it figured out concepts like mass and force, then Newton's second law, energy conservation, and the law of gravity. But here's the craziest part. It figured out mass in two different ways. One described how strongly gravity pulled on an object, the other how hard it was to change that object's motion. Then it checked that both gave the same number, and that connection is one of the foundations of Einstein's general relativity. For now, it just rediscovered the physics we already know, but imagine giving it data on dark matter, and it comes up with a new discovery.
